cand.title: CivicAction: The City Builders Dinner
cand.excerpt: High evidence specificity and dated organized hospitality activity; accessibility is discounted where the venue is already committed.
cand.ledgerVenue: The National Club, 303 Bay Street, Toronto

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Taylor Curran — Manager, Corporate Partnerships and Sponsorship, CivicAction; explicitly named for dinner partnerships, sponsorship and involvement, at taylor.curran@civicaction.ca. Korede Baiyewunmi — Event Coordinator, CivicAction; official biography covers event planning, logistics and stakeholder engagement, making her a relevant operational routing contact. The dinner page is attributed to Korede. Direct email for Korede is not published in the reviewed evidence; use events@civicaction.ca and request her. Neither person is verified as hotel-contract signatory.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced for Thursday, April 15, 2027, 5:30–9:00 pm, at The National Club, 303 Bay Street, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. These are event activity dates, not publication dates, and fall within the requested horizon. Expected attendance: approximately 150 invitation-only guests. No later dinner edition or exact 2028 dinner date was found. The separately referenced 2028 Summit is not a 2028 dinner announcement.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: the 150-person dinner is within the stated approximately 224-person banquet capacity, but this is only physical feasibility, not available business; its venue is already announced elsewhere. A downtown city hotel is more relevant than a resort for this regional, single-evening leadership gathering. The realistic Radisson role is individual VIP/executive stays or a small guestroom allocation if non-local guests exist—not 150 guestrooms, a buyout or assumed convention overflow. The regional guest focus and 5:30–9:00 pm programme do not establish overnight demand. The hotel’s official page states “Restaurant and Lounge closed until further notice”; banquet catering must be separately verified before proposing future dinners or receptions.
findings.venueCommitments: The National Club, 303 Bay Street, Toronto, Ontario, Canada, is the published 2027 venue. Its own description places it in downtown Toronto’s Financial District: Toronto proper and within the downtown territory, not Harbourfront or a resort. Treat this as a published venue commitment, not proof of a signed contract or an open venue requirement. It is a private business/social club with overnight rooms, not a conventional competing hotel.
findings.historicalRotation: No earlier same-name City Builders Dinner edition was verified; annual recurrence and destination rotation are unproven. A distinct CivicAction Partner in Action event was listed for September 23, 2026 at The National Club. This supports an existing organizer–venue relationship only; it is not a historical edition of this dinner. The 2019 and 2023 Summits cited on the dinner landing page are also different events.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. Neither official dinner page names a housing bureau, host hotel, hotel room block, booking link, accommodation buyer or open hotel RFP. There are no edition-specific hotels to enumerate. The event page directs: “For general event inquiries or event-related questions, please contact: Events Team: events@civicaction.ca”; this is an inquiry route, not a published lodging-sourcing method. The National Club separately advertises “Six overnight accommodation bedrooms, including one suite.” Its generic member-benefits page lists “St. Regis - Accommodation” and St. Regis Hotel valet benefits; neither establishes a City Builders Dinner booking commitment. No published dinner peak-room or room-night figure was found.
findings.organizationStructure: CivicAction is the named event organizer and civic nonprofit/charitable-sector convenor, not a corporate event agency, PCO or DMC. Its FY2024–25 annual report distinguishes the nonprofit Greater Toronto CivicAction Alliance from its charitable Leadership Foundation, while reporting an advancing transition/merger toward one charitable entity operating as CivicAction. The report does not establish the precise legal contracting entity for this dinner; confirm it before contracting. No external PCO/DMC is identified on the dinner pages.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The National Club is the incumbent dinner venue and advertises six overnight bedrooms, including one suite; no evidence shows those rooms are reserved for this event. The St. Regis reference is a generic club benefit, not an event room block. No sourced sellout, accommodation shortfall, overflow referral or competing hotel commitment was found. Radisson should not claim overflow merely because 150 people are invited.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Taylor Curran at taylor.curran@civicaction.ca, copying events@civicaction.ca and asking for Event Coordinator Korede Baiyewunmi. Acknowledge The National Club as the announced April 15, 2027 venue. Ask whether any non-local invitees, honourees or executives require overnight stays, whether the club bedrooms or another hotel already cover them, and who sources/pays for lodging. Only if unmet demand is confirmed, offer an appropriately sized guestroom proposal; do not quote an invented block. Separately ask about later dinner editions, venue-review timing and smaller leadership meetings. Verify hotel catering capability before offering food-and-beverage events.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2027 dinner venue capture is constrained by the published National Club commitment and invitation-only attendance. Guestroom sourcing remains unconfirmed, not open and not verified as committed elsewhere. The public events inbox and named partnership contact provide an inquiry pathway; neither proves purchasing access or lodging demand.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Conditional relationship-development prospect only. No verified annual dinner cycle, future dinner RFP, 2028 dinner date or rotation policy was found. Ask whether later dinners or smaller leadership gatherings will consider alternative downtown venues. The dinner landing page links its impact to a 2028 Summit, but this is a separate programme and must not be recorded as a confirmed future dinner or as demand for this hotel.
